prompt:
You are a senior information designer and editorial typographer who sets data tables for high-quality publications (statistical yearbooks, reference works, financial reports, technical documentation) in many writing systems, including Chinese. You judge by looking at the real rendered result.

Judge a table layout on all of these levels, in this order of necessity but as one whole:
1. correctness — every character visible, structure intact, nothing clipped or overlapping;
2. readability — natural line breaks, words/numbers/identifiers/semantic units kept whole, continuous reading;
3. function — easy to look up, compare, locate and understand the information for this table's real reading tasks;
4. visual order — alignment, grouping, hierarchy, consistent scale for elements with the same role;
5. visual rhythm — proportion, density changes, distribution of white space, spatial relationships;
6. overall aesthetics — balance, restraint, naturalness, harmony.
Do not assume that equal widths, symmetry, minimum height, the fewest lines, the golden ratio or any fixed proportion is good in itself; decide from this table's function, content and reading task, and look for counter-examples to your own rules.

Table: [val2] العربية · ترويسة متعددة المستويات (language ar, right-to-left: column 1 is on the RIGHT).
Grid: 4 columns × 5 rows. Row headers: yes.
Merged cells: "المحافظة" spans 1 col × 2 row; "عدد المدارس" spans 2 col × 1 row; "ملاحظات" spans 1 col × 2 row.
Measured content facts (text px at 17px font, padding excluded):
  col 1: header "المحافظة" · longest unbreakable unit 74px · widest one-line content 74px
  col 2: header "عدد المدارس › حكومية" · longest unbreakable unit 54px · widest one-line content 54px
  col 3: header "عدد المدارس › خاصة" · longest unbreakable unit 42px · widest one-line content 42px
  col 4: header "ملاحظات" · longest unbreakable unit 80px · widest one-line content 355px
Each column adds 21px of padding+border to its text width.
Viewport: 480px wide (dashed pink box in the renders). The table, including its 1px outer border, must be at most 480px wide (column widths sum to at most 479px); no horizontal scrolling. A table exactly 480px wide fits.
Fixed: content, font, 17px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. Only the column widths are designed; row heights follow from them.

You are continuing your synthesis. Shown after the overview: s0A, Layout P, Layout Q.
Measured facts:
s0A: column widths [100, 76, 65, 238] px · table 480×250 px · row heights [39, 39, 66, 39, 66] · column headers on >1 line: 0/5 · tallest cell 2 lines · measured breaks inside a word: 0 · fits the 480 px viewport (no scrolling)

Layout Q: column widths [100, 80, 70, 229] px · table 480×250 px · row heights [39, 39, 66, 39, 66] · column headers on >1 line: 0/5 · tallest cell 2 lines · measured breaks inside a word: 0 · fits the 480 px viewport (no scrolling)

Look again at the renders. Critique each, then propose up to 3 further refinements, or set "done": true if further changes would not bring a meaningful improvement.
